identity.name: load_centreline
identity.description: Loads Toronto's centreline street network (LineString, 4326) from the CKAN zipped shapefile into toronto_centreline by a staged full replace: one transaction creates a LIKE-INCLUDING-CONSTRAINTS temp table, inserts the validated rows, deletes the whole table and re-inserts from the staging table.

why_lock.text: Spec 47 §A.5 row 63. The spec's 65 collided with enrich-parcels; 63 is the next free gap and the shell keeps `ADVISORY_LOCK_ID = 63` textually (§5.4), so descriptor and shell cannot drift.

guard_why.text: A whole-table replace has no per-row predicate to guard on; class-C plan Fold F3 makes `guard: none` the honest declaration, and its `grandfathered.json` entry (Rule 9) is orchestrator-added.

idempotent_rerun_why.text: Every run DELETEs and re-inserts every staged row, so a byte-identical re-run still rewrites all ~47K rows (and their serial ids) — `zero_writes` is unachievable by construction under a full replace.

why.text: One pipeline.withTransaction carries all four statements — CREATE TEMP ... INCLUDING CONSTRAINTS (F-S11), staged INSERT, DELETE, INSERT...SELECT. They must commit together: a committed DELETE with a rolled-back re-insert empties the network enrich-centreline reads.

replay_why.text: Every run is an UNCONDITIONAL whole-table replace: the DELETE removes all ~47K rows and the INSERT…SELECT re-stages them from the temp table, so the source must be replayed in full and the prior contents carry no per-row reuse. This is the natural replay mode for class-C staging_full_replace with retract:"all" on a source the loader owns end-to-end (toronto_centreline is written by this step alone), and it is why the crash posture is force_full_on_next_run (LC-D5).

why.text: Four statements reach the database: CREATE TEMP TABLE, the batched staged INSERT, the DELETE, and the INSERT...SELECT back. The batched geometry validation is a pure SELECT and writes nothing.

on_prior_run_error_why.text: LC-D4 PIN. Legacy `.catch((err) => { pipeline.log.warn` degrades a failed prior read to "first run", so every drift ratio reads by definition. warn_row carries that non-failing posture (additive row on the error path only); it flips to fail_step at ④a.

why.text: Live catalog 2026-09-24: relrowsecurity=true with ZERO policies (migration 227 class-B default-deny) and the write works only via rolbypassrls. Under a non-bypass role the DELETE and INSERT...SELECT affect 0 rows with no error, so the verdict reads PASS.
The planar geometry GIST index the proximity joins read through; without it a centreline lookup degrades to a sequential scan over the whole street network.
The geography GIST index enrich-centreline joins through (its ST_DWithin over geom::geography); the planar index cannot serve that predicate.

on_row_error_why.text: A street whose geometry the validation cannot reduce to a valid LineString is dropped and counted, and the load continues — the tolerance is bounded by the declared FAIL-severity check `centreline_geometry_skipped_pct` (LC-D8: a single-member MultiLineString residue is a pinned DEFECT, so the dropped count is the liveness evidence, never a silent pass). The row is a counted loss, not a run-stopper: the source is 47K streets and one unrepairable line must not empty the network enrich-centreline joins.

on_check_error_why.text: Every check here reads a value the library already measured (acquired.*, prior.centreline_load.*), so a check that throws is a library defect, not an upstream condition — it must redden the run rather than drop its row. The one class-C exception is deliberate: `centreline_count_drift_pct` is scored at `when: "pre_write"` so its FAIL (or a WARN on the F-C1 arm via `on_warn: "skip_write"`) skips the write entirely rather than failing a transaction already opened.

why.text: The legacy `push('dataset_source_license', LICENSE_URL, 'INFO')` [READ load-centreline.js:410] freezes the licence in force at acquisition into the audit table: the centreline is redistributed open data and the licence is part of the provenance record. Legacy pushed it unconditionally on every path, so the row is the push's own successor.

expect.reports: the gate decision that ended the run, or null on a full load

why.text: The tier-1 (last-modified/etag) and tier-2 (content-hash) skip reasons travel in THIS row's detail, matching the legacy `push('centreline_load_skipped', …)` at BOTH :448 and :498. DS4: a skip and a no-op load must be distinguishable in the audit table — the consumer gate reads completed rows and needs the reason a run did nothing, so the skip is reported, never inferred from silence.

LC-D7. A standing `CENTRELINE_ACCEPT_FEATURE_COUNT_DRIFT` silently disarms the FAIL bound on every future run, so the row fires whenever the env is set — including runs that never needed rescuing [READ load-centreline.js:412-413]. The legacy pushed this only when the env was '1'; a declared check emits PASS at 0 (the ravines Fold D precedent) so silence can no longer mean both 'not set' and 'nobody looked'.

A CDN that strips both HTTP cache validators disables the pre-acquisition gate entirely: every run then downloads the 117 MB archive and leans on the content hash alone [READ load-centreline.js:441]. That is safe but not free, and it must be visible rather than inferred from a bandwidth bill. The legacy pushed this WARN only when the HEAD succeeded with no validator; a declared check emits PASS at 0 (ravines Fold D precedent).

checks.retighten_when: never — the centreline is re-published daily and an age leg above 7 days is a legitimate publisher cadence, not a defect; this row is a standing WARN (R-H) and retires only if the source's cadence is proven static

why.text: LC-D13 / R-H standing-WARN posture. The threshold is read in compute via `datasetAgeStatus(headAgeDays, config.centrelineSkipCheckThresholdDays)`'s successor — `load_centreline_dataset_age_warn_days` (seed 7, the daily-publish cadence knob) — never a bare literal [READ load-centreline.js:444, :52]. The legacy pushed INFO below the bound and WARN above it; this row carries the WARN so the age of a daily-published source that legitimately exceeds 7d reads as a STANDING WARN, never as a conversion defect.

expect.reports: every parsed DBF record, before filtering

why.text: The denominator of the L25 filter ratios: `acquired.rows_read` is every parsed record [READ load-centreline.js:508]. Legacy pushed it INFO on every path, so a declared check's PASS at 0 is the additive successor (the landing compare names these additive PASS rows) — measured 64385 on the last audited load.

expect.reports: source features whose CENTREL2 would not coerce to a positive integer key

why.text: LC-D2 / LC-D9. `acquired.bad_key_count`: a feature whose CENTREL2 is absent, non-numeric or <= 0 is dropped by the parse and never fabricated into a row, so it is a street that silently stops being in the network [READ load-centreline.js:509]. WARN, NEVER FAIL — the legacy WARNs, and LC-D9 records that the library coerces the key BEFORE shapeRecord so a renamed-key terminal is `failed_acquisition` (the staged-rows floor's `fail_check`), not this row. Legacy pushed only when > 0; a declared check emits PASS at 0 (ravines Fold D precedent).

expect.reports: source features carrying no geometry at all

why.text: LC-D17 attribution order. `acquired.null_geometry_count`: the LIBRARY counts null geometry BEFORE shapeRecord runs, whereas the legacy counted it AFTER the L25 classify [READ load-centreline.js:510]. Same WARN posture, the ordering is the documented divergence — a null-geometry record is invisible to `centreline_geometry_skipped_pct`, which measures only what ST_MakeValid could not repair over features that HAD a geometry, so without this row a source shipping empty records reads as a smaller dataset rather than a lossy one. Legacy pushed only when > 0; a declared check emits PASS at 0 (ravines Fold D precedent).

expect.reports: included features whose FEATURE_CODE is outside both the include and exclude sets, loaded with feature_code_desc_normalized = 'unknown_operator_review'

checks.retighten_when: never while the publisher still ships an unclassified street class — measured 1 on run 1471 and 1 in the PRE capture, so the population is standing, not zero; this WARN retires only once the publisher fixes the code and the count holds 0 across two consecutive loads (R-H)

why.text: LC / L25 unknown-code arm [READ load-centreline.js:552-557; docs/specs/01-pipeline/62_source_centreline.md:301-305]. `acquired.shaped_tags.unknown_feature_code` counts features the L25 classifier could neither include nor exclude; the loader keeps them with the sentinel `feature_code_desc_normalized = 'unknown_operator_review'` and WARNs [READ load-centreline.js]. This is a STANDING WARN (R-H): measured 1 on run 1471 and 1 in the PRE capture, so a non-zero row is the expected steady state, not a regression — the retighten condition is the publisher classifying the code, not a code change here. Legacy pushed only when > 0; a declared check emits PASS at 0 (ravines Fold D precedent).

expect.reports: included features whose JURISDICTION is 'unknown' (federal segments are dropped, not counted here)

checks.retighten_when: never while the publisher leaves segments with JURISDICTION 'unknown' — measured 94 on run 1471 and 97 in the PRE capture, so the population is standing; retires only once the publisher populates the field and the count holds 0 across two consecutive loads (R-H)

why.text: L25 jurisdiction arm [READ load-centreline.js:559-563; docs/specs/01-pipeline/62_source_centreline.md:307-308]. `acquired.shaped_tags.unknown_jurisdiction` counts included features whose jurisdiction is the literal 'unknown' — they are LOADED (unlike 'federal', which the classifier drops) and flagged for operator review. STANDING WARN (R-H): measured 94 on run 1471 and 97 in the PRE capture, so this is the expected steady state, never a conversion defect; the retighten condition is the publisher populating the field, not a change here. Legacy pushed only when > 0; a declared check emits PASS at 0 (ravines Fold D precedent).

expect.reports: source features whose CENTREL2 key repeats a key already seen; the dedupe keeps the FIRST occurrence and drops the rest

why.text: LC-D2 / Spec 62 corrected to the code at c2f [READ specs/01-pipeline/62_source_centreline.md edge-case table :358 'FAIL with clear error (D2 routed for JS-side pre-check enhancement)']. `acquired.duplicate_key_count` counts repeated CENTREL2 keys in one acquisition. WARN, NEVER FAIL: the SPEC's edge-case table words it 'FAIL', but the CODE dedupes — it keeps the first occurrence and drops the rest without raising — so the declared severity follows the CODE, not the spec prose (this is the Spec 62 correction recorded at c2f). Legacy pushed only when > 0; a declared check emits PASS at 0 (ravines Fold D precedent).

expect.reports: features that survived the L25 classify AND the duplicate-key dedupe — the row count the write stages

why.text: `acquired.feature_count` is the post-L25, post-dedupe count — the legacy `kept.length` [READ load-centreline.js; docs/specs/01-pipeline/62_source_centreline.md:1195]. INFO: it is the numerator of the geometry-skip ratio and the count the drift check 13 diffs against the prior run, but it is a purely DESCRIPTIVE counter here (no negative direction, cannot reach WARN/FAIL — Rule 5), so the declaration is the close of the legacy INFO push, whose silence used to mean both 'zero' and 'nobody looked'.

expect.of: this run's feature_count_filtered vs the prior run's centreline_load.feature_count_filtered

order_guarantee.guarantee: The L7 count-delta check must FAIL BEFORE any write: a source that suddenly carries half as many streets is a publisher error, not a legal road-network change, and the operator override CENTRELINE_ACCEPT_FEATURE_COUNT_DRIFT=1 ENABLES execution but NEVER suppresses the FAIL row — so the abort must land at the pre_write gate, before the DELETE opens a transaction that would empty the network enrich-centreline reads.

why.text: L7 count-delta [READ load-centreline.js; docs/specs/01-pipeline/62_source_centreline.md:323]. `load_centreline_count_drift_fail_pct` (seed 0.5) is the operator knob; `limit` carries the seed default and `limit_from_config` the runtime override (Rule 3). The string grammar 'pct <= X' is `definitions.bound` — PASS at <= X is EXACTLY the legacy `countDeltaPct > config...` FAIL inversion, so PASS/FAIL is byte-identical to the legacy arm. Computable from `ctx.acquired` + `ctx.prior` alone (when:pre_write contract). The override entry is `override.feature_count_drift` — it enables execution on a flagged run, it never rewrites this row's status. blocking:false (PIN, DO NOT FIX — plan D-8): the FAIL row exits 0 today, matching the legacy posture.

expect.of: features the ST_IsValid + ST_MakeValid pass could not reduce to a LineString, over feature_count_filtered

order_guarantee.guarantee: Spec 62 §3.5 makes > 5% unrepairable geometry an ABORT: FAIL the run and return BEFORE entering pipeline.withTransaction, so no transaction state can dangle and the pre-existing toronto_centreline is preserved untouched. This check is scored at when:pre_write for exactly that reason — a FAIL row here with no active override skips the write entirely (no transaction is opened).

why.text: L8 / LC-D15 [READ specs/01-pipeline/62_source_centreline.md:318 'L8 abort-before-DELETE: ... return without entering withTransaction'; LC-D8 PIN, the single-member MultiLineString residue]. `load_centreline_invalid_geometry_fail_pct` (seed 0.05) is the operator knob (Rule 3). NO override: legacy has none — a > 5% skip rate is always fatal. The row's detail carries the capped dropped centreline ids (the ravines LR-D1 shape), so the dropped set is inspectable without a second query. blocking:false (PIN, DO NOT FIX — plan D-8): the FAIL is verdict-bearing, the run still exits 0 as today.

expect.violation_when: zero carried rows AND ctx.prior is null

order_guarantee.guarantee: The F-C1 guard runs in JS BEFORE pipeline.withTransaction begins (Spec 62 §3.7: 'Check happens in JS BEFORE this transaction begins'): on a FIRST run (no prior) with zero carried rows there is nothing to insert, and letting the DELETE open would empty the network for a publisher-side empty archive — so the abort must land before the transaction, with the target untouched.
order_guarantee.anchor: F-C1 dual-mode (L15 / H-v1.3.2): zero-temp on subsequent run

why.text: Spec 62 §3.7 F-C1 dual-mode FIRST-RUN arm [READ specs/01-pipeline/62_source_centreline.md:339; legacy load-centreline.js:567-571 `if (!hasPriorRun) { push('f_c1_empty_temp_guard_fired', true, 'FAIL') }`]. A NEW id here (the legacy used one metric name for two arms — declared deviation, c2a4): the bound is EMPTINESS (carried rows == 0), NEVER `sources_centreline_floor` — plan §2 row 17 / §11 note records that the legacy fires this only at 0, and assert_data_bounds owns the floor. The conjunct on `ctx.prior == null` is what separates this from check 16's later-run arm. blocking:false (PIN, DO NOT FIX — plan D-8).

expect.violation_when: zero carried rows AND a prior run exists

order_guarantee.guarantee: The F-C1 subsequent-run arm (Spec 62 §3.7 / L15) fires BEFORE any write and PRESERVES the target: the table is left exactly as the prior run left it and the run completes WARN — so the gate must refuse the write (on_warn: skip_write) rather than open the DELETE/INSERT transaction on a zero-row temp stage.
order_guarantee.anchor: F-C1 dual-mode (L15 / H-v1.3.2): zero-temp on subsequent run

why.text: Spec 62 §3.7 F-C1 subsequent-run arm (LC-D14) [READ specs/01-pipeline/62_source_centreline.md:339; legacy load-centreline.js:573-579 WARN + `delete_skipped_empty_guard: true` and a preserved table]. INGESTOR prerequisite 0h third arm: `on_warn: "skip_write"` makes this WARN row refuse the write at the pre_write gate (no transaction opened, target untouched, write counters 0) while the run COMPLETES with the WARN — the observable 'warn and preserve' the legacy encoded in compute. The `features_inserted: 0` emit is PINNED and flips at ④b. blocking:false (PIN, DO NOT FIX — plan D-8).

expect.reports: features whose geometry the validator unwrapped out of a GeometryCollection to reach a LineString member

checks.retighten_when: any non-zero value — the counter is 0 in 8/8 measured runs (LC-D8 PIN), so the first non-zero is a real source-shape change and must be looked at, not absorbed by an INFO row (R-H)

why.text: `acquired.geometry_collection_extracted` (LC-D8 PIN; 0 in 8/8 runs) [READ load-centreline.js]. Operator ruling Q2: this is a DECLARED CHECK over the runner's own counter, not a library option — the extraction happens as the validator walks a GeometryCollection for a LineString member, so the count is read from the runner, never re-derived. INFO keeps the verdict IDENTICAL to legacy: a GeometryCollection that yielded a member already counts as SKIPPED by validatorCounterDelta in the legacy arm, so promoting this row would double-count and change the verdict. Purely descriptive (Rule 5).

expect.reports: true when the F-C1 preserve path refused the write — either the pre_write WARN gate or the executor's own empty-temp guard

why.text: The legacy INFO row on the F-C1 preserve path (`delete_skipped_empty_guard`) [READ load-centreline.js:579; docs/specs/01-pipeline/62_source_centreline.md:614]. Reads `written.write_skipped_pre_write_warn === true || written.replace_skipped_empty_guard === true`: the first is the pre_write gate's own row (check 16's `on_warn: skip_write` arm, INGESTOR prerequisite 0h), the second is the executor's independent empty-temp guard — defense in depth. INFO: descriptive only, it records WHICH guard fired, it does not gate.

expect.reports: rows the write path inserted — equals the staged row count on a full replace, 0 when a guard skipped the write

why.text: `written.inserted` [READ load-centreline.js — the legacy `features_inserted` emit]. INFO: on this class-C staging_full_replace the INSERT...SELECT re-inserts every staged row after the DELETE, so the count is the load's own size — descriptive, no negative direction (Rule 5). It is PINNED at 0 on the F-C1 preserve path (check 16) and flips at ④b.

expect.reports: rows the full-replace DELETE removed — the table's PRE-state size on a committed run

why.text: `written.deleted` — the DELETE rowCount, which on a full replace equals the PRE-state table size [READ load-centreline.js; assessment §7 'inter-run coupling']. INFO: it is the evidence that the replace is complete, and its inter-run coupling (this run's deleted ↔ prior run's inserted) is exactly what the PIN records — the number is descriptive, it gates nothing (Rule 5).

LC-D7. When the city genuinely re-publishes the network at a different size, an operator must be able to accept the drift for ONE run. The acceptance enables execution and NEVER suppresses the FAIL row — the FAIL verdict is still recorded on `centreline_count_drift_pct`, so the rescue is auditable rather than erased (operator ruling A-5). Legacy read the env as the literal `=== '1'` [READ load-centreline.js:412]; the runner's declaration is the legacy read's successor, and the standing-override WARN row `centreline_override_feature_count_drift_present` fires whenever the env is set, including runs it never rescued.

RETIRED per Spec 124 R-AZ (the argv-seam rule) / LC-D6 + LC-D11, on the address_points precedent. A debug affordance let an operator run the full parse→filter→validate→staging pipeline against a manually-fetched local zip when the CKAN large-resource endpoint was unservable, skipping the HEAD + download entirely. The frozen shell acquires through `inputs.reads.externals[]` and the fixture tier replaces the local seam for tests. The retirement is declared, not silent: with it goes the only fs/argv seam the step had, and the `centreline_local_zip_override` WARN row it used to push.

deviations.adjudicated_by: operator ruling, Spec 124 R-AZ / LC-D6, LC-D11

deviations.from: the legacy `push('centreline_head_error', …, 'WARN')` on the HEAD-failure path (load-centreline.js:437)

why.text: The HEAD 4xx/5xx path (§3.9: WARN + proceed to download, do NOT skip on failure) is now the library's zero-row HEAD-error WARN row, driven by the declared `inputs.reads.externals[0].on_head_error: "warn_row"`. LC-D: the row keeps the legacy posture (a failed HEAD never halts, the download still runs and the content hash still gates) — the runner emits it, so the metric name `centreline_head_error` is retired into the library row rather than re-pushed by the step.

LC-D9 / LC-D10. The legacy download/zip/parse failure pushed a FAIL row and returned `{ failed: true }`; under the archetype that path is the library's `failed_acquisition` fail-error terminal (no write attempted, temp root cleaned). The metric name `centreline_acquisition_error` is retired into the terminal. The RENAMED-KEY case (CENTREL2 absent/renamed) does NOT land here: LC-D9 records that the library coerces the key BEFORE shapeRecord, so a renamed key ends at the staged-rows floor's `fail_check`, not at `failed_acquisition`.

LC-D15, on the ravines LR-D1 precedent. The per-feature WARN rows made the audit table's row count bounded only by the feature count (47K streets). The dropped ids now travel as CAPPED detail on the `centreline_geometry_skipped_pct` row (with the exact dropped count and a truncation flag beside them), so the dropped set is inspectable without one row per dropped feature and the reader is never misled about how much was lost.

RETIRED per LC-D12 (the address_points 525K-row precedent): the runner issues ONE validator call over the whole validated set rather than 5K-row chunks. The chunking was a pre-conversion planner-memory workaround; the converted library sizes its own validator input and the counter semantics (`geometry_collection_extracted`, `invalid_geometry_skipped`) are unchanged, so the drop is a mechanism retirement, not a behaviour change.

deviations.from: one legacy metric name (`f_c1_empty_temp_guard_fired`) reused for BOTH F-C1 arms (load-centreline.js:567 FAIL and :573 WARN)

why.text: The F-C1 dual-mode guard's FIRST-RUN arm (no prior run, zero carried rows) now carries its own id `f_c1_empty_temp_guard_fired_first_run` (FAIL), separate from the subsequent-run arm `f_c1_empty_temp_guard_fired` (WARN + on_warn:skip_write). The legacy reused one metric name for two arms with different severities, so the audit table could not tell a build-blocking empty source from a preserved-table no-op; the split is additive and the ordering/liveness are unchanged.

deviations.from: the legacy conditional-only WARN pushes (bad id, null geometry, unknown code, unknown jurisdiction, duplicate, override)

why.text: The ravines Fold D precedent: every legacy `if (x > 0) push(...)` WARN is declared as a CHECK that also emits PASS at 0, so silence can no longer mean both 'zero' and 'nobody looked'. Applies to `centreline_bad_centreline_id_count`, `centreline_null_geometry_count`, `centreline_unknown_feature_code_count`, `centreline_unknown_jurisdiction_count`, `centreline_duplicate_centreline_id_count` and the standing-override row. Severity and bound are unchanged; only the observable-at-zero posture is added.

deviations.from: the legacy ad-hoc `CENTRELINE_LOCAL_ZIP`-era override set (no force-reload hatch)

why.text: `CENTRELINE_FORCE_RELOAD` is ADDED as `override.force_run`: the retired local-zip seam was the only way an operator could bypass the staleness gates, so with it gone a deliberate full reload (a source the tier-1/tier-2 gates keep skipping) needs a declared force env. It is named in this descriptor and mirrored in `recovery.force` at c2a5, matching the ravines `RAVINE_FORCE_RELOAD` shape the conversion added there (declared deviation on that step).

deviations.adjudicated_by: plan LC-D6 (force hatch) / ravines conversion precedent

deviations.from: the legacy phase order, where L8 geometry validation ran only on the write path after the drift gate

why.text: The geometry validation now runs BEFORE the drift gate (read-only, on the ravines Fold C / LR-D9 precedent): both `centreline_geometry_skipped_pct` and `centreline_count_drift_pct` are scored at `when: "pre_write"` between the read-only validation and the first write statement. The observable consequence is that a drift-FAIL run ALSO measures the skipped geometry — the validation is a pure SELECT, so this adds observability and moves no write. No spec guarantee is retired by this ordering (the legacy abort-before-withTransaction for L8 is preserved).

deviations.from: the legacy config source `loadMarketplaceConfigs(pool, MARKETPLACE_KEY)` + `validateConfig(logicVars)` (load-centreline.js:402-403, MARKETPLACE_KEY 'source-centreline')

why.text: LC-D3: the six knobs are now `config.logic_variables[]` registered logic variables resolved through `ctx.config`, not a marketplace-config read inside the step body. `centrelineMinFeatureCount` is KNOWINGLY RETIRED rather than declared — it was never read (the L7 count-delta is a ratio check, and the F-C1 guard's bound is the staged-row count, not a floor); declaring it would be a phantom consumer (Rule 3's purpose, not its letter). The other five keep their seed defaults byte-equal to the pre-externalization literals.

limitations.what: Null-geometry source records are counted by the LIBRARY before `shapeRecord` runs, whereas the legacy counted them AFTER the L25 classify — so the `centreline_null_geometry_count` number is measured at a different point in the pipeline than the pre-conversion counter. Same WARN posture, different ordering (LC-D17).
limitations.measured: LC-D17; 0 on run 1471 and 0 in the PRE capture, so the ordering divergence is currently invisible in the numbers — a null-geometry record that the L25 classify would have dropped is now visible to the count

limitations.what: source_id is coerced through the key path and re-keyed as a JS number in the validation join, so a BIGINT above 2^53 would lose precision and miss its own validation row — counted as skipped rather than loaded. load_ravines carries the same class of limitation.

LC-D8 single-member MultiLineString residue: a feature the validator can only recover as a single-member MultiLineString (not reduced to a plain LineString) is a pinned DEFECT, not a silent pass — the extraction of a LineString member is counted at `centreline_geometry_collection_extracted` and the dropped remainder by the geometry-skipped counter.
limitations.measured: LC-D8 PIN; `centreline_geometry_collection_extracted` = 0 in 8/8 measured runs, so the residue has never been observed live

limitations.what: LC-D16 CORRECTED at c2e (VERIFY-INT-4, measured against the real `ledgerPipelineName`): there is NO divergence. `ledgerPipelineName(descriptor, chainId)` falls back to `Object.keys(descriptor.execution.invocation)[0]` ("sources") whenever `chainId` is falsy — which is exactly the standalone case (`chainId = process.env.PIPELINE_CHAIN || null`) — so a standalone run reads/writes under the SAME `sources:load_centreline` ledger name as an in-chain run, byte-identical to the legacy hard-coded `PIPELINE_NAME = 'sources:load_centreline'` (load-centreline.js:44). The original LC-D16 text ("reads the un-prefixed ledger name `load_centreline`") was never measured against the real function and is retracted; a standalone/in-chain prior read never diverges for this step.

LC-D18 (found at ② POST capture, 2026-09-25) — `scripts/lib/step/index.js`'s generic `verdict === 'WARN'` terminal-selection branch calls `selectTerminal({kind:'success', status:'completed_with_warnings'})` with NO discriminator, so it picks the FIRST/only declared success terminal at that status regardless of WHICH check(s) actually warned. This descriptor declares only ONE such terminal (`loaded_preserved_empty_guard`), so a genuine full load whose only WARN rows are the standing `centreline_unknown_feature_code_count`/`centreline_unknown_jurisdiction_count` (or any other non-F-C1 WARN) is ALSO labelled `loaded_preserved_empty_guard` in `records_meta.terminal` — a misleading STRING (implies the F-C1 preserve/empty-guard path fired when it did not). Does NOT affect correctness: `records_meta.centreline_load` (the 18-key frozen contract `enrich_centreline` actually reads), the audit_table rows, the verdict, and every write/counter are all correct and unaffected — `terminal` is a summary label outside that frozen contract. The proper fix is a LIBRARY change (the WARN branch needs its own discriminator, the same shape the FAIL branch already gets via `unaccepted[0]`) that benefits every converted INGESTOR with more than one `completed_with_warnings` success terminal — out of scope for this conversion's zero-behaviour-change mandate (Spec 121 §4.3) and filed as a Spec 124 §7 rung (d) library-prerequisite candidate, not a per-step hatch.

interrupted_why.text: LC-D5 truthful posture, and this is NOT the usual retract:"all" argument. Every load_centreline run IS a full replace executed inside ONE step-scoped transaction (write_discipline.txn_scope "step": CREATE TEMP … INCLUDING CONSTRAINTS, the staged INSERT, the DELETE, then INSERT…SELECT). A kill mid-run therefore cannot leave a hole — the transaction either fully rolls back (prior table byte-intact) or fully commits — but the NEXT run's staleness gate cannot see that either way: a crash is not a completed run, so the tier-1/tier-2 gates and the L7 prior-read would resolve against a stale-or-absent baseline and read "unchanged" or "first run", silently retiring the count-drift bound. Claiming resume would be a lie (there is no checkpoint), and claiming none would let the gate under-read a killed run. force_full_on_next_run is the honest posture: the successor run replaces the whole table again, unconditionally. Class-C plan F2; LC-D5 / the ① ledger's truthful-posture row.

before_image_why.text: OPERATOR RULING R-M / LG-17 (2026-08-28). The generic before-image mechanism (scripts/lib/step/write.js writeBeforeImage) mirrors a retraction's write_discipline.scope predicate as a SELECT — it structurally requires a scope. load_centreline's only target is class C staging_full_replace with write_discipline.scope "none": the retraction is an UNCONDITIONAL whole-table DELETE, not a scoped predicate, so there is no WHERE-clause for the generic mechanism to mirror and nothing to capture as a row-level before-image. The prior table's contents are recoverable the way a full replace is always recoverable — by re-running against the prior source version via CENTRELINE_FORCE_RELOAD — and the retraction's SIZE is already the evidence row `centreline_features_deleted` (written.deleted). Genuinely out of this conversion's scope, declared rather than silently ignored.

why.text: A full replace has NO per-row update: the write is DELETE-the-table-then-INSERT…SELECT, so `written.updated` does not exist and the frozen producer block pins `features_updated: 0` forever (LC-D14 / the legacy literal `records_updated: 0` in skeletonLoadMeta, load-centreline.js:687). The truthful source is therefore the emit's own field, read back from `records_meta.centreline_load.features_updated` — the value enrich_centreline already consumes — rather than a counter the write path never produces. `written.updated` would be a phantom; this is the load counting its OWN per-row updates as the zero it declares.
